recent.summary: Anthropic's record $81.3B IPO dominated the session, lifting AI/cloud and semi names (NET +5.7%, AMD +5.3%, AMZN +3.8%, AVGO +3.6%) while NVDA fell -2.9% as post-CEO-exit governance concerns offset an earnings beat. Energy cratered on US-Iran oil transfer curbs (XOM/CVX/OXY all ~-4–5%), UNH collapsed -10.2% on CMS Medicare Advantage clawback proposals, and crypto-adjacent names sold off on hawkish Fed October minutes signaling more rate hikes. Broad indices barely moved as intense sector rotation offset gains and losses.

A broad risk-off selloff accelerated into a 6th consecutive S&P 500 decline, with the AI/semiconductor complex hit hardest by a triple catalyst: a Hunterbrook short-seller report linking AMD firmware to a blacklisted Chinese firm (-7.7%), a California AG subpoena adding legal/governance overhang to NVDA (-ongoing), and Anthropic's IPO pop failing to revive the AI trade. SELL discipline dominated the session with NVDA SELL +6.5% in favor and UNH SELL +15.2%, while only CVX held green on Middle East energy risk premium from a Houthi strike on Riyadh. BUY positions in AVGO, AMZN, and COST are holding but underwater pressure is mounting across the full book.

A broad risk-off acceleration has pushed the Nasdaq to its worst week since 2020 and both major indexes into correction territory, driven by a triple catalyst: an SEC accounting probe into Nvidia (per Reuters), a disappointing Anthropic IPO, and massive bearish options bets confirmed in chip stocks (per CNBC). The AI/semiconductor complex is in full rout — NVDA -14%, MARA -18.6%, MU -13.9% — while defensives and energy hold firm, with healthcare (UNH +2.84%) and consumer staples (WMT +1.52%) acting as the only working rotation plays. SELL discipline continues to dominate the track record (58% win rate vs. 28% BUY), with the open NVDA SELL now +19.6% in profit as the standout call of the cycle.

Jensen Huang's reinstatement as NVDA CEO triggered a historic short-squeeze and Nasdaq's best session since April 2025, with NVDA surging +31.5%, MU +19%, and INTC +16% on massive AI infrastructure sentiment reversal. New BUY signals were initiated on NVDA, MU, and MSFT, while energy positions in XOM and CVX were cut as oil sits near 3-month lows and capital rotates hard into growth. The prior NVDA SELL thesis (governance/SEC risk) is now fully resolved; energy BUY discipline flagged as a repeated weak spot with CVX -6.4% and XOM -1.9% on open positions.

Risk-off sentiment resurged as the semiconductor/AI complex (MU -11%, AMD -8.9%, NVDA -5.9%) gave back Monday's euphoria-driven gains amid analyst downgrades, inflation data caution, and PC/auto memory mix concerns. Capital rotated firmly into defensives, with LMT and JNJ leading on Houthi geopolitical escalation and healthcare staples demand, while SAP outperformed on EU tech rotation away from US semis. The BUY book took heavy damage with a 21% hit rate on longs, reinforcing a disciplined posture of cutting losses early and awaiting confirmed bases before re-entry.

Pre-Thanksgiving risk-off trade hit the AI/semiconductor complex hard (NVDA -3.9%, MU -4.5%, ORCL -5.1%), compounded by an S&P Global credit warning and ongoing governance/regulatory scrutiny on Nvidia, while the Nasdaq staged a dramatic intraday reversal from -1,100 Dow points to close higher. Defensives and low-capex tech held firm, with LMT (+2.1%) buoyed by dual geopolitical catalysts (Kyiv missile strike + Houthi escalation), META (+3.4%) rotating as a safe-haven versus capex-heavy semis, and AAPL continuing its divergence (+30.61% YTD vs. NVDA -21.35%). SELL discipline remains the dominant edge this cycle, with MU SELL +4.5% and NVDA SELL +3.9% both in the money, while the low BUY hit rate (23%) demands a higher confirmation bar for new longs.

AI/semiconductor stocks remain under sustained multi-day pressure (NVDA -21% from highs, MU SELL +4.5%, ORCL at 52-week low with CDS stress at 360bps), while defensives and low-capex mega-cap tech (LMT, AAPL, META) continue to outperform as safe-haven rotations dominate a Nasdaq correction. SELL discipline is the only proven edge this cycle with a 23% BUY hit rate, as macro tape overrides single-stock fundamentals in risk-off conditions. Mideast escalation (Aramco Jazan refinery attack, Hamas-Israel, Kuwait site) sustains defense premium, and holiday-week thin volume is driving erratic futures swings.

weekly.summary: A BofA AI bubble warning, CoreWeave credit stress, and VIX spiking above 22 triggered a four-session, $260B+ risk-off unwind crushing high-multiple AI, cloud, and crypto names (PLTR, SNOW -8%+, MSTR -9.6% with added MSCI removal headwinds, MARA -9.6%). Capital rotated decisively into Defense (RTX +3.7%, LMT +3.6%) and Energy (CVX +2.6%) on Middle East escalation via Yemen missile strikes and a US SPR solicitation, while AAPL held as the lone resilient core-tech name on iPhone demand, Chinese subsidies, and Berkshire support. Core calls — **BUY RTX, LMT, AAPL; SELL PLTR, MSTR** — remained fully intact across all sessions.

**Week Summary (3 sentences):**

AI/cloud and cybersecurity (DDOG, NET, AMZN) were the dominant BUY themes, fueled by SpaceX compute demand, PHP vulnerability spikes, and Iran escalation-driven infrastructure bids — with NET and DDOG delivering strong gains — though the Nasdaq's worst session since June, triggered by chipmaking supply warnings and META AI spending fears, crushed semis (AMD -8.1%, INTC -8.0%) and pulled the broader growth complex below its 50-day MA. Defense was a major early-week driver via NOC's $110B backlog, LMT's ~7% F-35 surge, and RTX read-across BUYs, but geopolitical risk-premium fading and Ukraine peace talk resumption sparked a late-week rotation out of the sector, while capital shifted defensively into cybersecurity and energy infrastructure as Iran escalation entered day two. MSTR and PLTR SELLs were badly burned (-12.2% and -8.4%) by crypto regulatory clarity and the AI rebound, AAPL was downgraded on foldable sell-the-news risk, and AMZN BUY was closed at -5.5% and flipped to SELL ahead of earnings — leaving NET (+6.0%), DDOG (+3.6%), and LMT (+2.4%) as the week's cleanest working calls.

**Summary:** AI infrastructure euphoria rapidly reversed into a sector-wide reckoning — early BUY validation from ORCL, Azure, and Anthropic's IPO gave way to INTC's -28.6% collapse, GOOGL's worst-ever single-day drop (-12.6%) on structural search fears, and broad semi weakness (NVDA, AMD, AVGO, DDOG all deeply underwater), leaving the Nasdaq on pace for its worst month in over a year. Capital rotated decisively into Defense (LHX +6.84%, RTX, LMT outperforming on $11B missile awards and DoD spending), Energy (XOM, CVX bid up on Hormuz tanker fires and Saudi evacuation orders), and Consumer Staples (WMT), while Big Tech earnings sharply divided the tape with AMZN on WATCH amid AI capex overhang. Key active calls are BUY LHX, RTX, LLY; high-conviction SELL GOOGL and META; a hawkish Fed hold at 3.75–4.0% and tighter sell discipline on AI longs represent the principal forward risks.

**Summary:** The two-week period was dominated by extreme semiconductor volatility — an initial brutal chip selloff (MU -17.5%, AMD -17.3%, TSM -10.8%) driven by AI spending fears and regulation concerns was followed by a sharp rebound (AMD +11%, TSM +6.3%) confirming AI capex demand remains intact, while mega-cap tech (MSFT, AAPL) and post-election defensives lagged the recovery. Key calls saw AMZN emerge as the standout long (+8.3%), PLTR SELL extend gains to +11.6%, AMD BUY cut at -16.4% loss, and MSFT BUY exited on a fresh negative catalyst, with NVDA re-entered at oversold levels into the bounce. Overall portfolio conviction remains cautious with a challenged 47%/33% win rate, as cloud earnings risk (DDOG -14.4%) and ongoing sector rotation complexity continue to pressure execution.

**Week Summary:** The dominant macro theme was NVDA's CEO governance crisis, which catalyzed a broad semi selloff (AMD -8.75%, AVGO -4.76%) while keeping NVDA and AMD SELL signals deep in the money (+8.8% each), with capital rotating into defensives (WMT, CVX, META) and selective semi alternatives (AVGO, GOOGL flagged as cleanest BUY setups despite sector pressure). An HSBC sector downgrade compounded the risk-off wave alongside hot CPI and rising yields, weighing on high-multiple AI/mega-cap names (MSFT, META, AMZN underperforming even on green tape), though underlying AI/infrastructure demand signals remained intact via hyperscaler GPU accumulation. Key discipline takeaways: treat governance/leadership risk as an immediate exit trigger, size down high-multiple AI names into yield-surge environments, require multi-source confirmation before entries, and monitor the META SELL (now a loss from $628.77) for a close, while geopolitical energy risk (Hormuz Strait, Houthi strikes) reinforces the CVX BUY thesis.

**Weekly Summary:** A US rule restricting China's AI chip access drove a sustained risk-off selloff, hammering semiconductors and AI names (NVDA, AMD, MU, AVGO down 4–10%) and software (CRM -9.5%), with VIX surging four consecutive days as investors rotated aggressively from tech into defensives. Defense (RTX, LMT) and select names (AVGO, WMT, COST) were the week's standout survivors, boosted by Middle East escalation and NVDA's earnings beat validating AI infrastructure demand—though export-curb headwinds and CEO succession uncertainty kept semis broadly pressured. Active SELL signals on NVDA (+12.6%) and AMD (+13.8%) are significantly outperforming a weak BUY book (37% hit rate), reinforcing the bearish semi/AI thesis, while new BUYs on RTX, AVGO, and AMZN (White House AI champion + Anthropic IPO optionality) reflect the week's key rotation trade.
